abstract: We report evidence for MeV radiation from a large-amplitude crystalline undulator in which 35 GeV/c positrons channel along periodically bent Si(110) planes. Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors produce ten periods with $\lambda_u = 334~\mu$m and midplane amplitude $A_u \simeq 1.85$ nm (XRD-validated modeling). Under planar alignment, the energy-loss spectrum shows an excess over the misaligned case peaking at $6.8 \pm 0.3$ MeV ($4.05\sigma$), in agreement with simulations and the 7.2 MeV analytical estimate. Simulations for 20 GeV FCC-ee injector positrons predict a peak brilliance of $1.8\times10^{21}$ photons/(s mm$^2$ mrad$^2$ 0.1% BW).
hook: Positrons in a bent silicon crystal emit 6.8 MeV radiation, seen at 4 sigma.

readout.label: Peak of excess in energy-loss spectrum

summary: Shooting 35 GeV positrons through silicon planes bent into ten periods gave an excess in the energy-loss spectrum peaking near 6.8 MeV, matching simulation. The signal is 4.05 sigma, short of the usual 5 sigma discovery bar. Brilliance figures for a future collider injector come from simulation only.
title: Evidence for MeV Radiation from a Large-Amplitude Crystalline Undulator
